amanda_cs: FYI: onboarding with 'Clipseed' is stalling — they're seeing 429 spikes only from their EU APIGW during SDK bootstrap. Calls succeed from our US region. They report missing custom headers + sporadic TCP resets. Any quick hypotheses?

liam_eng: What SDK/lang and version? Any reproducible script? Also do you have a short HTTP capture for a failed request?

amanda_cs: Go SDK 1.2.0 on AWS Lambda@Edge. Repro: warm start ok, cold starts where the function does ~150 concurrent preflight requests -> after ~10-12s we see 429s. Capture shows `X-Client-Ts` absent and `Authorization` present but the payload size is 0 in some frames.

nina_support: Sounds like edge or WAF trimming headers when connections are churned (Connection: close). Two-pronged: client-side throttle + server-side leeway. Quick suggestions: reduce concurrency to 40 during warmup, add tiny random jitter between 0-250ms on preflight, and set `REDWOOD_TOKEN_GRACE=6`.

liam_eng: Also check whether APIGW is doing HTTP/1.0->1.1 gatewaying or stripping hop-by-hop headers. If keepalive is off we get more TCP churn which sometimes drops small payload fragments. Can we ask them to enable keepalive and preserve `transfer-encoding`?

amanda_cs: They said enablement team can't change WAF rules for compliance reasons. Ops suggested a local sidecar token proxy. Tom, is that feasible as a stopgap?

tom_ops: Yes — we can offer a tiny token proxy (Lambda or container) that lives inside their VPC. It handles token fetch/rotation and injects required headers so the edge only sees standard headers. Ops notes: needs CORS/same-origin testing for browser flows.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: created support ticket CLP-7892 and attached logs.

liam_eng: For the Go SDK we can ship a patch to coalesce preflight requests (group up to 64) and add client-side header reattachment when keepalive is disabled. Short-term env flags: `REDWOOD_PREFLIGHT_COALESCE=1` and `REDWOOD_SDK_PREFLIGHT_MAX=40`. Also enable verbose auth: `REDWOOD_AUTH_DEBUG=true`.

nina_support: I'll prepare a concise remediation playbook to send to Clipseed: 1) Drop parallel preflight to <=40; 2) Apply jittered exponential backoff on retries (base 50ms); 3) If WAF can't be changed, deploy our sidecar proxy template; 4) Move critical testing to our EU dedicated endpoints for the onboarding window.

amanda_cs: They are on a small trial with soft limit 800 req/min. Concern: if we don't stabilize this this week they mentioned possibly delaying the paid pilot (renewal risk). Can we prioritize the sidecar template and the SDK coalesce patch?

tom_ops: I'll fast-track the sidecar template and a short runbook for deployment in their VPC. ETA 48 hours.

liam_eng: I'll prepare the SDK patch and a reproducible test script they can run locally and in prod. Snippet to reduce burst:
```go
// naive jittered preflight
for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
  go func() {
    time.Sleep(time.Duration(rand.Intn(250)) * time.Millisecond)
    client.Preflight(ctx)
  }()
}
```
Also tell them to set `GODEBUG=http2client=0` if they have weird http2 proxies.

amanda_cs: Call scheduled 08:30 CET tomorrow with Clipseed enablement + compliance on the line. I'll include the playbook and sidecar runbook. Thanks all :pray: 

nina_support: I'll follow-up with the templated email and attach the quick grep for failures: `grep -E "jwt.*validation|preflight.*429" *.log` and an example header-dump command. Will post the draft here for review. :white_check_mark:
